title: Challenge 5: Swap without SWAP Gate
storyScenario: Due to hardware architecture constraints on a superconducting chip, direct SWAP couplers are unavailable. You must swap registers using standard CNOT couplers.
description: Swap the states of Qubit 0 and Qubit 1 using ONLY three CNOT gates (no SWAP gate permitted).
targetGoal: If Q0=1, state becomes |01⟩. If Q1=1, state becomes |10⟩.

starterCode.qiskit:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_circuit():
    qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
    qc.x(0) # Initial state |01>
    # TODO: Three CNOT ladder
    qc.cx(0, 1)
    qc.cx(1, 0)
    qc.cx(0, 1)
    return qc
starterCode.cirq:
import cirq
q = cirq.LineQubit.range(2)
circuit = cirq.Circuit(cirq.X(q[0]), cirq.CNOT(q[0], q[1]), cirq.CNOT(q[1], q[0]), cirq.CNOT(q[0], q[1]))

testCases.name: Hidden: Prohibition of Native SWAP Gate

editorial.mathematicalProof: Three alternating CNOTs implement the boolean XOR swap algorithm: a=a⊕b, b=b⊕a, a=a⊕b, resulting in b and a exchanged.
editorial.algorithmicAnalysis: Giallar Rule R7 proves CX(0,1)·CX(1,0)·CX(0,1) ≡ SWAP(0,1) in universal unitary matrix algebra.

hints: Use the alternating control/target CNOT ladder: CX(0->1), CX(1->0), CX(0->1).
